1. # CLAUDE.md
2. 
3. This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.
4. 
5. ## What this is
6. 
7. An IntelliJ Platform plugin ("Codeowls") that adds first-class editor support for `CODEOWNERS` files (GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket). It registers a `CODEOWNERS` language for any file literally named `CODEOWNERS`. Despite the template README describing Kotlin, **all production and test code is Java** under `src/main/java` and `src/test/java`.
8. 
9. ## Commands
10. 
11. - Build: `./gradlew build`
12. - Run all tests: `./gradlew test`
13. - Run one test class: `./gradlew test --tests 'net.wolfig.codeowls.matcher.CodeownersGlobTest'`
14. - Run one test method: `./gradlew test --tests 'net.wolfig.codeowls.matcher.CodeownersGlobTest.methodName'`
15. - Launch a sandbox IDE with the plugin: `./gradlew runIde`
16. - Verify plugin compatibility against target IDEs: `./gradlew verifyPlugin`
17. 
18. The IntelliJ Platform SDK and target IDE (`intellijIdea("2025.3.5")`) are pulled by the `org.jetbrains.intellij.platform` Gradle plugin; the first build downloads a large SDK. `.run/` holds equivalent IDE run configurations (Run Plugin, Run Tests, Run Verifications).
19. 
20. Note: the user runs tests themselves — do not auto-run `./gradlew test` to verify changes unless asked.
21. 
22. ## Architecture
23. 
24. Everything keys off one shared, handwritten lexer. There is **no PSI tree / parser** in the usual sense — `CodeownersParserDefinition` exists to register the file type and highlighting, but semantic work is done by re-lexing text directly. When changing token semantics, the lexer is the single source of truth and most other components consume its output.
25. 
26. Layers, bottom-up:
27. 
28. - **`lexer/`** — `CodeownersLexer` (extends `LexerBase`) is a stateful, line-oriented lexer. Every line is classified as empty / comment / GitLab section header (`[Name]`, `^[Name]`, with optional `[N]` approval count and default owners) / rule (`pattern owner...`). Token categories live in `CodeownersTokenTypes`. Both syntax highlighting and rule parsing drive this same lexer.
29. 
30. - **`matcher/`** — the ownership model, IDE-independent and the most heavily unit-tested code.
31.   - `CodeownersRuleParser.parse()` is the **only** place lexer tokens become the rule model. It applies GitLab section semantics: a section header's default owners and approval count are inherited by rules in that section that name no owners of their own; a rule's own owners override. The owners stored on each `CodeownersRule` are the *effective* owners after inheritance.
32.   - `CodeownersGlob.compile()` turns a CODEOWNERS glob into an anchored regex over forward-slash, project-relative paths. Semantics follow GitHub's documented rules (a subset of gitignore) — see its Javadoc before touching `*`/`**`/`?`/anchoring behavior. Leading `!` (GitLab negation) is stripped here; callers handle negation. Resolution is **last-match-wins**.
33. 
34. - **`statusbar/CodeownersService`** — project-level `@Service` that locates the active CODEOWNERS file by walking a file's parent chain trying `CANDIDATE_PATHS` (`.github/CODEOWNERS`, `CODEOWNERS`, `docs/CODEOWNERS`, `.gitlab/CODEOWNERS`, in that precedence), parses it (cached by modification stamp), and resolves the matching rule. It is intentionally **listener-free**: it reparses lazily on stamp change; the status bar widget owns the VFS/PSI listeners and drives re-resolution to avoid a service↔UI feedback loop.
35. 
36. - **Feature packages** (each roughly one `plugin.xml` extension): `highlighting/` (syntax + color settings page), `folding/` (GitLab section blocks), `completion/` (path, owner, and section-name completion; owners come from the file, Git-history contributors, and built-in GitLab roles `@@developer`/`@@maintainer`/`@@owner`), `inlay/` ("N files" hints + toggle action), `navigation/` (gutter line marker for matched files, Ctrl/Cmd+Click owner → GitHub/GitLab page resolved from the Git remote), `inspection/` (flags rules matching no file or shadowed by a later rule, with quick fix), `refactoring/` (rewrites rule paths on file move/rename), `suggestion/` (confidence-ranked owner suggestions for un-owned files).
37. 
38. All extension points are wired in `src/main/resources/META-INF/plugin.xml`; user-facing strings live in `messages/CodeownersBundle.properties`.
39. 
40. ## Tests
41. 
42. - Framework is **JUnit 4** (`@Test`/`@Before`/`@After`, not JUnit 5). Tests follow Arrange / Act / Assert.
43. - Pure-logic tests (`matcher/`, lexer) run standalone. Anything touching PSI, completion, editor actions, or project services uses the IntelliJ `CodeInsightTestFixture`.
44. - **Fixture setup must go through `IdeaTestFixtureFactory.createCodeInsightFixture(builder.getFixture())`** (built from `createLightFixtureBuilder`) — not a bare `IdeaProjectTestFixture`. Some fixture operations must run on the EDT (see existing tests' use of `EdtTestUtil`). Copy the setUp/tearDown pattern from an existing fixture test (e.g. `CodeownersCompletionTest`) when adding one.
45. - Configure content with `fixture.configureByText(CodeownersFileType.INSTANCE, ...)`; `<caret>` markers in the text drive completion/caret-position assertions.
46.

+# Copilot instructions for Codeowls
+
+## Project and commands
+
+Codeowls is an IntelliJ Platform plugin that provides editor support for GitHub, GitLab, and Bitbucket `CODEOWNERS` files. Although the Gradle build applies the Kotlin plugin and the template README refers to Kotlin, production and test code is Java under `src/main/java` and `src/test/java`.
+
+- Build: `./gradlew build`
+- Run all tests: `./gradlew test`
+- Run one test class: `./gradlew test --tests 'net.wolfig.codeowls.matcher.CodeownersGlobTest'`
+- Run one test method: `./gradlew test --tests 'net.wolfig.codeowls.matcher.CodeownersGlobTest.methodName'`
+- Launch the plugin in a sandbox IDE: `./gradlew runIde`
+- Verify plugin compatibility: `./gradlew verifyPlugin`
+
+The first Gradle run may be slow because the IntelliJ Platform plugin downloads the target IDE SDK (`intellijIdea("2025.3.5")`). Equivalent IDE run configurations are in `.run/`. There is no dedicated lint task. Do not automatically run the full test suite unless the user asks; the user runs tests themselves.
+
+## Architecture
+
+The handwritten, stateful `CodeownersLexer` is the shared source of truth for CODEOWNERS syntax. It classifies each line as whitespace, a comment, a GitLab section header, or a pattern plus owner tokens. Both highlighting and semantic features consume these tokens.
+
+`CodeownersParserDefinition` intentionally creates only a single file-root node; there is no meaningful custom PSI tree or generated parser. Features that need CODEOWNERS semantics re-lex file text instead of traversing custom PSI elements.
+
+`CodeownersRuleParser.parse()` is the only translation point from lexer tokens to the matcher model. It applies GitLab section behavior: default owners and approval counts flow to rules in a section, while owners explicitly listed on a rule replace section defaults. Keep this model conversion centralized when adding token types or syntax.
+
+The IDE-independent matcher layer compiles CODEOWNERS globs into anchored regular expressions over forward-slash, repository-relative paths. `CodeownersGlob` follows GitHub's CODEOWNERS subset of gitignore semantics; read its Javadoc and tests before changing `*`, `**`, `?`, slash anchoring, directory matching, or GitLab `!` handling. Ownership resolution is last-match-wins.
+
+`CodeownersService` is the project-level ownership resolver. Starting from a target file, it walks ancestor directories and checks `.github/CODEOWNERS`, `CODEOWNERS`, `docs/CODEOWNERS`, then `.gitlab/CODEOWNERS` in that order. Parsed rules are cached by document/VFS modification stamp so unsaved edits are visible. Keep the service listener-free: UI components own VFS/PSI listeners and trigger lazy re-resolution.
+
+Feature packages such as completion, highlighting, navigation, inspection, refactoring, inlays, folding, explanation, and owner suggestions build on the lexer/matcher/service layers. IntelliJ extension points and actions are registered in `src/main/resources/META-INF/plugin.xml`; user-facing strings belong in `src/main/resources/messages/CodeownersBundle.properties`.
+
+## Codebase conventions
+
+- Use JUnit 4 (`org.junit.Test`, `@Before`, `@After`), not JUnit 5. Tests use Arrange / Act / Assert structure.
+- Keep pure lexer and matcher tests standalone. Code that touches PSI, completion, editor actions, or project services should use `CodeInsightTestFixture`.
+- Create fixture tests with `IdeaTestFixtureFactory.createLightFixtureBuilder(...)`, then `factory.createCodeInsightFixture(builder.getFixture())`; do not use a bare `IdeaProjectTestFixture`. Follow the setup/teardown pattern in `CodeownersCompletionTest`.
+- Configure CODEOWNERS fixture content with `fixture.configureByText(CodeownersFileType.INSTANCE, ...)`; use `<caret>` markers for caret-sensitive behavior.
+- Wrap VFS/PSI access in IntelliJ read actions where required. Run editor mutations and fixture operations that require the UI thread through `EdtTestUtil`, following nearby tests.
+- Preserve forward-slash, repository-relative path semantics across matching, completion, navigation, inspections, refactoring, and suggestions.
+- When token semantics change, update the lexer first and check every token consumer, especially `CodeownersRuleParser`, highlighting, completion, folding, inspections, navigation, and refactoring.
*** End Patch
